comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5807054385) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5807088782), checked at `cbb7a789`.

| Earlier finding | Status at `cbb7a789` |
|---|---|
| Escaped and invalid UTF-8 bytes grow past the limit after awk | **Resolved** for quotes, backslashes and control bytes. **Still present** for invalid UTF-8 in a UTF-8 locale (see below) |
| 500-file cap is not a byte limit | **Still present, narrower**: now only through the invalid UTF-8 route |
| Code comment and PR description overstate the protection | **Still present**: the new comment says the growth "is enforced in omarchy-menu-select" |
| Budget counts characters, not bytes, in a UTF-8 locale (awk) | Resolved earlier; unchanged |
| Only the newest 500 **or fewer** files are eligible | Resolved earlier in the PR description |
| Test expected `$real/clip.webm` | Resolved earlier; the test still passes |

**Verified:** The new check in `omarchy-menu-select` rejects oversized options from quotes, backslashes and control bytes with `options payload too large` (exit 1) in every locale tested, instead of the earlier `Argument list too long`. Ordinary menus produce payloads identical to `f9c706e3`, the `omarchy-menu-file` listing is byte-identical, and the PR's test passes at this head and still fails against the base `omarchy-menu-file`.

## The new size check counts characters, not bytes, in a UTF-8 locale

[`omarchy-menu-select:80`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/cbb7a789938fa5808ae2a34dd285c15ce3ece787/bin/omarchy-menu-select#L77-L84) measures `options_json_bytes=${#options_json}`. Bash documents `${#parameter}` as the length in characters, so under a UTF-8 locale it counts code points. `encode_json` writes U+FFFD (3 bytes) and other non-ASCII text as raw UTF-8, so the check undercounts exactly the invalid UTF-8 growth it was added to catch. This is the same character/byte distinction as the earlier awk finding, one step later.

Isolated runs at `cbb7a789` with the real `omarchy-menu-file` and `omarchy-menu-select`, synthetic file names:

```text
case (entries kept)                     JSON bytes  counted in UTF-8  C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8       LC_ALL=C
long CP1251 names (414)                    204,931            80,731  Argument list too long (126)  rejected (exit 1)
ASCII names in a CP1251 folder (321)       208,972            80,572  Argument list too long (126)  rejected (exit 1)
60 CJK chars + 40 control bytes (304)      141,361           104,881  Argument list too long (126)  rejected (exit 1)
120 quotes/backslashes per name (493)      140,013           140,013  rejected (exit 1)             rejected (exit 1)
```

The oversized JSON passes the check and fails at the second Perl call (lines 86 to 97), the same result as at `f9c706e3`.

**Impact:** In a UTF-8 locale, listings from `omarchy-menu-file` without ASCII escape growth count at most about 81,000 characters, so the check cannot trigger on them. Collections with long legacy-encoded names still make `omarchy-transcode` and `omarchy-games-retro-install` fail as before, and large lists of non-ASCII options passed directly to `omarchy-menu-select` are not bounded either. The reply's statement that U+FFFD expansion can no longer trip `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` holds only under a C locale.

**Suggested change:** Count bytes, for example `options_json_bytes=$(LC_ALL=C; printf '%s' "${#options_json}")`. In a disposable copy of this head, that one-line change rejected 500 CP1251 options with exit 1 under both UTF-8 locales, and small menus still opened. Measuring the length inside the first Perl call is an alternative. With either change, the comments in both scripts become accurate. The PR description still says a huge library "cannot blow MAX_ARG_STRLEN" and does not mention the select-side check.

**Optional test improvement:** The PR's only test replaces `omarchy-menu-select` with a stub, so the new check has no coverage. A test that stubs `omarchy-shell` instead and passes invalid UTF-8 options under `C.UTF-8` would fail at this head (exit 126) and pass with the change above (exit 1).

**Note on the new error:** The message goes to stderr only. `omarchy-transcode` is started from the menu and `SUPER + CTRL + PERIOD`, and `omarchy-games-retro-install` from the menu, both without a terminal. When the check triggers, no picker and no message appear, and `omarchy-games-retro-install` exits 0 through `|| exit 0`. The "clear select error" described in the reply is visible only when run from a terminal.

**Note on the 120,000 limit:** Lists whose encoded JSON is between 120,001 and about 130,900 bytes used to open and are now rejected. For example, 500 direct ASCII options with a 125,164-byte payload opened at `f9c706e3` and exit 1 at this head. Through `omarchy-menu-file` this needs heavily escaped names. The in-tree menus checked are far below this range.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up at `cbb7a789`, compared with `f9c706e3`. Isolated command-only runs used the real `omarchy-menu-file` and `omarchy-menu-select`, synthetic file names, the `C.UTF-8`, `en_US.UTF-8` and C locales, and a stub in place of the shell IPC hop that receives the real payload as an argument. The PR's test file ran by itself. Menu rendering, the real IPC transport and the full test suite were not run. The locale of real menu and keybinding launches was not observed: the main finding assumes a UTF-8 `LC_CTYPE`, which Omarchy's shell environment falls back to. Limits assume 4 KiB pages.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
